gates.reason: The metrics probe exposes its bearer token, disables TLS verification, and uses an unpinned container image.
This E2E harness contains no detector, recommendation, parser, provenance, or calculation claims.
This is test orchestration, not production hot-path code or a newly shipped runtime surface.
The command runner logs complete arguments, including the bearer token supplied by this batch's E2E test, and installer helpers apply remote manifests without integrity verification.
These test helpers do not produce recommendations or implement claim-bearing detector, parser, or calculation logic.
These utilities run during tests and setup, not on a production request or ingest hot path.

findings.title: Metrics bearer token is written to test and pod logs
findings.what: The TokenRequest bearer token is interpolated into the kubectl --overrides argument. Run then writes the complete argument vector to GinkgoWriter and repeats it in returned errors. The pod also runs curl -v, which emits request headers, including Authorization, into pod logs that the test retrieves. Anyone with access to CI output can recover a live Kubernetes credential.
findings.fix: Use the curl pod's projected service-account token from a mounted file instead of placing a fetched token in kubectl arguments, remove curl -v, and make Run redact recognized credentials from both normal and error logging.
findings.acceptance: Run the E2E test with a sentinel token and capture GinkgoWriter, returned errors, and curl-metrics logs; assert that none contains the sentinel or an Authorization header while the authenticated metrics assertion still passes.
findings.verifyNote: A second pass confirmed the token returned at e2e_test.go:188 is formatted into the pod override at lines 216-237; utils.go:53-57 logs and may return that entire argument, while curl -v at line 222 exposes request headers to the logs read at lines 252-256 and 314-320.

findings.title: Metrics probe explicitly disables TLS certificate verification
findings.what: The probe invokes curl with -k, so a successful test does not establish the identity of the metrics endpoint and permits interception by any endpoint presenting an arbitrary certificate.
findings.fix: Mount the metrics-serving CA into the probe and invoke curl with --cacert and the expected service DNS name, without -k.
findings.acceptance: The metrics E2E test passes with certificate verification enabled and fails when the endpoint presents a certificate signed by an untrusted CA or for the wrong hostname.
findings.verifyNote: The adversarial re-read confirmed -k is present in the only metrics request and no CA or other certificate-validation option is supplied in the pod specification.

findings.title: E2E workload executes a mutable latest-tag image
findings.what: Both kubectl run and the override select curlimages/curl:latest. The executed bytes can change between runs without a repository change, weakening reproducibility and allowing an upstream tag compromise to execute inside the test cluster.
findings.fix: Pin one reviewed curl image by immutable digest in both image fields, preferably through a single constant.
findings.acceptance: Inspect the generated pod and verify its image is an approved name@sha256 digest and that no latest tag remains in the file.
findings.verifyNote: A second pass confirmed both image declarations use the same mutable latest tag and neither supplies a digest.

findings.title: Installer helpers apply network-fetched manifests without integrity verification
findings.what: The helpers pass GitHub release URLs directly to kubectl create/apply. Versioned URL paths do not cryptographically verify the received content, so DNS, TLS, hosting, or upstream-release compromise can inject cluster-wide resources into the test cluster.
findings.fix: Vendor the reviewed manifests or download them to a temporary file, verify an allowlisted SHA-256 digest, and only then pass the verified local file to kubectl.
findings.acceptance: Installer tests demonstrate that the approved manifest digest installs successfully and a one-byte-modified manifest is rejected before kubectl executes.
findings.verifyNote: The adversarial pass confirmed both installers construct remote HTTPS URLs and hand them directly to kubectl; there is no digest, signature, or local-content verification in either path.
